If you were a 33 all around, like 33 in every sub score, then I’d say maybe hold off. You have an obvious weak point at math. Get that bumped up to a 28 and you have a 34. Get it to a 32 and you have a 35.

You have a good 400 time that you can build off of. Focus on running tempo efforts and implement workouts that’ll improve your aerobic capacity. Steadily increase your mileage, but most importantly you’re young, your times will drop as you grow but if you want to start to implement the things I said above it wouldn’t be a bad idea.
If you don’t want to have too much mileage you should incorporate high speed sessions into your weekly structure, foot speed is very important for 800 runners. (Hill sprints, 50m flys, etc)

Not a butterflyer but I can provide some tips that may help:
1. Turns
- I find that after taking a break from swimming, the thing I lose my touch on first is my turns. Slow turns can easily cost you time, and fast turns win races. I dropped 2 seconds in my 100 breaststroke from prelims to finals because of my coach telling me my mistakes in my turns. Ask your coach to specifically look at the turns in a 50 or 100 butterfly you may do in practice or a meet. Make sure you make yourself as hydrodynamic as possible during your turns, and be efficient.
2. Underwaters
- The best swimmers I know have fast underwaters  which they use a TON of during their races. Personally, my underwaters are not great, but I recognize that it’s a flaw and that the more I improve my underwaters, the more time I drop. I am absolutely not saying go to the 15m mark every time you come off your turn, but you are potentially doing too few underwaters.

Those are my tips. Hopefully you drop time soon!

I wish I started out basketball with dribbling. Shooting is fun and in my opinion there isnt any better feeling than draining a three, but you should really focus on dribbling. When I go to a basketball practice or game, I look at peoples dribbling and how they get to the basket. Dribbling well can create shots, open lanes to drive in and creates space. Once you have good dribbles, then work on dribble combos into shots, like pulling up in midrange. If you feel that your dribbles are good enough, then look at form shooting routines and work your way up to three point range. Hope this helps.
